steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Moist heat methods (use water or steam): boiling, simmering, poaching, steaming, braising, stewing. These are suitable for tougher cuts of meat and preserve moisture in foods.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dry heat methods (use fat, oil, or air): baking, roasting, grilling, frying (shallow, deep, stir). These create browning (Maillard reaction) and crispy textures.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Boiling: cooking in water at 100°C. Quick but can leach water-soluble vitamins (B and C) into the cooking water. Suitable for pasta, potatoes, rice.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Steaming: cooking over boiling water in a covered pan. Preserves nutrients (no contact with water), colour, and texture. The healthiest cooking method for vegetables and fish.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Categorise cooking methods as moist heat or dry heat — this structure earns marks. Always link a cooking method to its effect on nutrients: steaming preserves, boiling leaches, microwaving retains. For health comparison questions, rank methods: steaming > grilling > baking > shallow frying > deep frying. Know specific temperatures: boiling 100°C, simmering 85–95°C, poaching 70–90°C, baking 160–220°C.
